config.title: Model API success error via discriminated unions

intro.title: Model API success error via discriminated unions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple function that simulates fetching data from an API and returns a result that is either a success with data or an error with a message. You will learn to model these two possible outcomes using a TypeScript discriminated union, which is a type that can be one of several distinct shapes, each identified by a common property (like 'status'). This approach helps make your code more predictable and type-safe by clearly defining success and error states. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces, union types, and type narrowing to handle each case correctly. By the end, you'll understand how to represent and work with API responses in a robust, typed manner.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, handling API responses robustly is critical for user experience. For example, a dashboard fetching user data must clearly differentiate between a successful load (displaying charts), a network error (showing a retry button), and an empty state (suggesting initial setup). Using discriminated unions in TypeScript allows developers to model these distinct outcomes with type safety, ensuring the UI correctly renders loading spinners, success content, or error messages without runtime surprises. This pattern is essential in forms, data tables, and any component that interacts with backend services.

objectives: Construct a discriminated union type to represent API response states
Initialize state variables using the discriminated union type
Implement a function that returns different union members based on API conditions
Manipulate UI rendering logic to display content according to the current union member
Configure TypeScript type guards to narrow union types in conditional blocks
Integrate error handling by updating state with error union members
Apply pattern matching techniques to handle all possible union cases exhaustively

steps.title: Define discriminated union types for API response
steps.instruction: Define two TypeScript types: 'ApiSuccess' and 'ApiError', each with a 'status' discriminant property, and a union type 'ApiResponse' that combines them.
steps.hint: Create interfaces or type aliases with a literal 'status' property to distinguish between success and error states.

// Import React and useState from 'react' here

// Define ApiSuccess, ApiError, and ApiResponse types here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have three type definitions: ApiSuccess with status 'success' and data, ApiError with status 'error' and message, and ApiResponse as their union.
successCriteria: ApiSuccess and ApiError types are defined with discriminant 'status' properties, and ApiResponse is a union of both.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the discriminated union types for modeling API responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Ensure both ApiSuccess and ApiError have a 'status' property with literal values, and ApiResponse is their union.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the type definitions. Each should have a discriminant property 'status' with specific literal values, and ApiResponse should be a union type.

steps.title: Create main component with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ApiResponseDisplay with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to add TypeScript typing for the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ApiResponseDisplay is defined with TypeScript typing and returns null.
successCriteria: The ApiResponseDisplay component is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ApiResponseDisplay component with TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'ApiResponseDisplay' and has proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'ApiResponseDisplay' and added TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Initialize state with discriminated union
steps.instruction: Inside your ApiResponseDisplay component, initialize a state variable named 'apiResponse' of type ApiResponse with a loading state using useState.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with the ApiResponse type. Set the initial value to an object that matches the 'loading' case of your discriminated union.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with a union type
const [status, setStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'loading' | 'success'>('idle');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'apiResponse' properly typed as ApiResponse and initialized to represent a loading state.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with the ApiResponse type and an initial value that matches the loading case of the discriminated union.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly initialized the apiResponse state with the proper type and loading state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ApiResponse type and setting the initial value to represent a loading state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState with the ApiResponse type and set the initial value to a loading state object.

steps.title: Define handler to simulate successful API response
steps.instruction: Inside your ApiResponseDisplay component, create a function named simulateSuccess that returns an ApiSuccess object with mock data. Use the ApiSuccess type you defined earlier.
steps.hint: The function should return an object with a 'status' property set to 'success' and a 'data' property containing some mock data (like a string or number).
steps.expectedOutcome: A simulateSuccess function is defined inside the component, returning a properly typed ApiSuccess object.
successCriteria: The simulateSuccess function is defined with the correct name, returns an object matching the ApiSuccess type, and includes both 'status' and 'data' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a function that simulates a successful API response with proper typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns an object with both 'status' (set to 'success') and 'data' properties, matching the ApiSuccess type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The simulateSuccess function is missing or doesn't return a properly typed ApiSuccess object. Check the function definition and return value.

steps.title: Define handler to simulate error API response
steps.instruction: Inside your ApiResponseDisplay component, define a new function named simulateError that returns an ApiError object with a descriptive error message.
steps.hint: Create a function that returns an object matching the ApiError type you defined earlier. Include a 'type' property set to 'error' and a 'message' property with a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A simulateError function is added to the component, returning a properly typed ApiError object.
successCriteria: The simulateError function exists, returns an object with type 'error' and a message string, and matches the ApiError type structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a function that simulates an API error response with proper typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but check that it returns an object with exactly 'type: "error"' and a 'message' string property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The simulateError function is missing or doesn't return a correctly structured ApiError object. Review the ApiError type definition.

steps.title: Create markup structure for response display
steps.instruction: Inside the ApiResponseDisplay component, return a div container with a heading that says 'API Response Display' and a paragraph placeholder that says 'Response will appear here'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (null) with JSX that includes a div, an h2 heading, and a p element with the specified text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic JSX structure with a heading and placeholder text, ready for later conditional rendering of API response data.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing an h2 with text 'API Response Display' and a p with text 'Response will appear here'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic UI structure. The heading and placeholder paragraph provide a foundation for displaying API response data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your JSX includes both the h2 heading with 'API Response Display' and the p element with 'Response will appear here' inside a div container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return JSX with a div containing an h2 heading and a p element. Check that you've replaced the null return with the proper JSX structure.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering based on discriminated union
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add conditional rendering that checks the 'status' property of the apiResponse state and displays appropriate content for each case (success, error, or loading).
steps.hint: Use a switch statement or if/else blocks to check apiResponse.status and return different JSX for each case. Remember to handle all possible status values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display different content based on the apiResponse status, using TypeScript's type narrowing to safely access properties.
successCriteria: Conditional rendering is implemented that checks apiResponse.status and displays appropriate content for success, error, and loading cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering using the discriminated union's discriminant property.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some conditional logic, but make sure to handle all possible status values (success, error, and loading).
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering doesn't properly check apiResponse.status or handle all cases. Review how to use TypeScript's type narrowing with discriminated unions.

steps.title: Add success and error buttons and wire handlers
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add two buttons: one labeled 'Simulate Success' that calls simulateSuccess when clicked, and another labeled 'Simulate Error' that calls simulateError when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the existing heading and paragraph. Use onClick handlers to call the appropriate functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two interactive buttons appear in the UI that will trigger different API response states when clicked.
successCriteria: The component contains two buttons with labels 'Simulate Success' and 'Simulate Error', each with onClick handlers calling simulateSuccess and simulateError respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added buttons to trigger both success and error API responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have both success and error buttons with proper onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly implemented. Check that you have two buttons with appropriate labels and onClick handlers.

steps.title: Add reset functionality
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named resetResponse that sets the apiResponse state back to its initial loading state.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setApiResponse with an object containing status: 'loading'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A resetResponse function is defined that will reset the apiResponse state to loading.
successCriteria: The component contains a resetResponse function that sets apiResponse to { status: 'loading' }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the reset functionality. This completes the API response modeling with discriminated unions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your resetResponse function properly sets the apiResponse state back to the loading state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetResponse function isn't defined correctly. It should update the state to return to the initial loading state.
